traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, p. 120): joints broadly obovate, 8 to 20 cm long; spines none, or rarely a few on the upper areoles; glochids brownish.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a low clump under 40 cm tall of pads 5 to 20 cm long, fanning out from the base. Bright magenta flowers along the top of the pads in spring. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: 20 to 40 cm. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: blue-grey pads, often purple-tinged, with no long spines; the sunken areoles carry dense tufts of reddish-brown glochids. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): its tepals on a spiral (16 by hand: no flora counts them, and USDA GRIN records 9 to 22 petals on accessions of Opuntia, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read) on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, from the characters of Cactaceae by the rules at the flowering plants. Its 200 stamens by hand, the most a flower draws, for the numerous ones every flora gives.
